absent: Full descriptor allocation, expansion and install paths beyond duplication target handling.
Pipe data transfer, polling, resizing and I/O serialization semantics.
Complete coredump orchestration choosing among socket, file and other destinations with fallback.
Pidfs mount setup, inode operations and access checks beyond allocation and coredump recording.
Full definitions and sizes of core structures such as file tables, files, inodes, dentries and coredump parameters.
Detailed error values and userspace visible effects for all failure paths.
Consumer side ordering and visibility rules for pidfs attributes and pipe state beyond observed barriers.

findings.text: Pidfs exposes an allocator that builds a file object for a given process identifier with caller flags, backed by a reused or newly created anonymous dentry from stashed storage. It rejects stale marking from caller flags and always opens the resulting dentry read-write while preserving selected pidfd control bits.

A helper builds a filesystem path from a stash pointer and mount, reusing a live dentry when available and otherwise creating and publishing a new anonymous dentry. Ownership of caller data transfers to the filesystem on success, and the returned path holds counted references to dentry and mount.

A generic opener creates an empty file for supplied flags and credentials then performs the VFS open step on a caller path, releasing the file and reporting failure as an error pointer when the open step fails.

Pipe creation yields two file objects sharing one pipe state, one readable and one writable, both marked stream oriented and nonblocking capable. It optionally enables notification queue support and disables permission and pre-content notification while keeping legacy notification behavior.

File cloning derives a second file sharing path and mapping of a base file under new flags and operations. Stream marking adjusts file mode to indicate sequential access without seek or positioned operations.

Pipe support exposes allocators and releasers for pipe state and inode, plus accounting of buffered pages against a user. Allocation applies system and per-user limits with privilege exemptions, while release drains buffers, notification state, preallocated pages and user references.

Pidfs records coredump outcome into per-process attributes, combining a dumpability derived mask with a dumped marker and publishing signal details. A mapper translates dumpable levels for owner, privileged and disabled cases into user, privileged and skip coredump categories.

Coredump destination selection is split between a socket based handshake with userspace and a direct file creation path with safety checks. The socket path is available in one build variant and reports unavailability in the other, while the file path validates size, location, link, type, ownership and writability before handing the file to the caller.

A successfully reserved descriptor keeps a null table entry until its matching install step completes. An entry that is marked open yet still null indicates a concurrent reservation in progress and must not be overwritten.

Open, close-on-exec and full-word tracking stay coherent: setting an open entry also sets or clears its close-on-exec mark per caller request and marks the containing word full when all its bits become set. Clearing close-on-exec only acts when the bit is currently set.

An anonymous stashed dentry permanently records the address of its stash slot and its inode privately stores the caller data pointer used at creation. After path construction both linkages are expected to hold.

A fresh pipe inode starts dirty to avoid dirty list movement, carries FIFO type with owner read-write mode and current filesystem identity and timestamps, uses anonymous pipe operations, and references pipe state expecting two files with one reader and one writer.

Descriptor duplication is entered holding the file table lock and releases it on every exit path before any blocking close of a displaced file. The displaced file close happens after unlock, while reference acquisition and table publication happen under lock.

Stash pointer reads and compare-exchange publication occur under an RCU guard, with liveness acquired through a lock reference check that rejects dead dentries. Failed reuse retries publication until a live entry is installed or adopted.
Decrement of pipe file count and clearing of the inode pipe pointer are serialized by the inode lock, with final teardown of pipe state performed after unlock only when the count reaches zero.
Newly allocated pipe state initializes reader and writer waits and a dedicated mutex with a custom comparison function for lock ordering.
The file descriptor table as observed holds an array of file pointers with a maximum size, bitsets for open descriptors and close-on-exec marks, and a bitset summarizing fully occupied words.

Pipe state as observed includes buffer array with ring size and usage limits, accounted count and owning user, reader and writer waits and counters, reader and writer tallies, file count, optional notification queue and preallocated page cache plus a serializing mutex.

Per-process pidfs attributes as observed carry a coredump mask, a flag word with a coredump completion bit, and signal number and code describing the coredump cause. Publication orders attribute writes before setting the completion bit.

The coredump socket handshake exchanges a request describing supported size and option mask and expected acknowledgement size, and an acknowledgement carrying its own size, selected mask and reserved field. Single markers signal acceptance or specific size and option errors.

Pipe creation proceeds through inode allocation, optional notification setup, write end allocation, read end cloning and mode finalization. Each failure stage unwinds only resources acquired so far, including pipe buffers, user accounting and inode references.

Path construction first attempts to adopt an existing stashed dentry, releasing caller data on reuse. On miss it creates a new inode and anonymous dentry, publishes it with custom or default stashing, discards the loser on concurrent win, then forms the path with counted mount reference.

Coredump socket handling connects, announces capabilities, peeks acknowledgement size, validates size bounds, fetches the full acknowledgement, checks size consistency, flag subset, exclusive selection and reserved zero, then confirms acceptance. Any validation failure emits a distinct marker and aborts; completion later waits for peer closure and shuts down the write direction.
An alternate build provides inert wait and shutdown operations and a socket entry that always reports failure, effectively disabling socket based coredump delivery while keeping call sites unchanged.

Duplication to a target that is concurrently reserved but not yet installed must fail with busy status rather than installing and losing to the racing installer. Target index handling also applies speculation bounds protection before table access.

Direct coredump file creation enforces minimum size, fully qualified path for privileged dumpable mode, exclusive creation without following links, single link, hashed regular file, preserved owner and strict permissions, writability and truncation. Nonprivileged mode first removes any prior file, while privileged mode resolves the path from the initial root.

Socket based coredump validates peer identity against the dumping process, rejects unknown acknowledgement sizes and flags, requires exactly one delivery mode among userspace, kernel and reject, and reports full queue or connection failure distinctly.

Descriptor duplication honors a close-on-exec request bit and reports contention with a busy error. Pidfd files are forced read-write, preserve thread and autokill control bits from caller flags, and strip stale and exclusive-truncate bits during open.

Pipe ends propagate nonblock and direct request bits where applicable, start as write-only and read-only pair, and gain stream, nowait and nonotify-permission modes. Notification pipe creation requests an extra queue initialization step.

Pipe sizing starts from a default buffer count capped by a system maximum for unprivileged callers, then downgraded to a minimum on soft per-user excess and rejected on hard per-user excess, with system resource and administration capabilities granting exemption.

Coredump socket negotiation advertises kernel, userspace, reject and wait capabilities with minimum and current acknowledgement sizes, while pidfs coredump masks distinguish user, privileged, skip and dumped states.
Coredump files are created write-only with create, no-follow, large-file and exclusive semantics under strict owner-only permissions.
Dentry open serves as a filesystem entry for instantiating a file from a mounted path, requiring a valid mount and returning either a usable file or an error pointer.

Pipe pair creation and pidfs file allocation serve as entries for anonymous pipe and process handle instantiation, each returning zero or a file on success and a negative or error-pointer failure otherwise.
Pidfs coredump recording serves as the entry invoked during coredump handling to publish dump outcome and cause into process attributes for later userspace observation.
